page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 236 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mix of capabilities. Single-threaded operations are highly efficient, with gzip compression achieving top-tier performance at 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression registering a strong 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory write benchmarks show limitations; stress-ng multi-core performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression are categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth write for large blocks is also weak at 23.77 GB/sec, though large block read-only bandwidth remains average at 43.94 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores fall within the average tier.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff between strong single-core execution and weaker multi-threaded scaling. This makes the instance highly suitable for workloads that rely on single-threaded throughput, such as lightweight web serving, which achieves an average throughput of 8.72 GB/sec, and Redis key-value stores, which perform at an average of 8.24 million SET operations per second. It is also appropriate for general-purpose applications, database operations, and basic file processing, but less suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded computing tasks.
